items.title: A.I. and Our Economic Future (Charles I. Jones, NBER w34779)
items.desc: Revised June 2026. Frames scenarios for how AI — likely the most transformative technology of the modern era — could reshape economic growth, wages, and welfare, from modest productivity gains to transformative change.

items.title: Understanding Firms' AI Efforts and Their Economic Impact (Tania Babina, NBER w35123)
items.desc: Reviews firm-level datasets measuring AI adoption and shows that measurement is central: different AI datasets can lead to materially different conclusions about AI's economic impact.

items.title: The Urban-Rural Divide in the Age of Artificial Intelligence (arXiv econ.GN)
items.desc: Distinguishes automation exposure (concentrated in routine work) from AI exposure (concentrated in cognitive work) and assesses their diverging effects on regional labor markets.

items.title: Some Simple Economics of AGI (arXiv)
items.desc: A simple framework for how artificial general intelligence would affect output growth, the labor share, and wages.

items.title: Measuring What Cannot Be Surveyed: LLMs as Instruments for Latent Cognitive Variables in Labor Economics (arXiv)
items.desc: Proposes using large language models to measure latent cognitive variables in labor economics that traditional surveys cannot capture.

items.title: Large Language Models for Asset Pricing: Learning from Earnings Calls (Zhang & Zhou, SSRN)
items.desc: Posted May 2026. Applies LLMs to earnings-call transcripts to extract pricing-relevant signals for the cross-section of stock returns.

items.title: Option Return Predictability via Large Language Models (Liu et al., SSRN)
items.desc: Posted April 2026. Shows LLM-extracted textual information predicts option returns.

items.title: Large Language Models and Stock Investing: Is the Human Factor Required? (SSRN)
items.desc: Evaluates ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Perplexity stock recommendations across prompting strategies: LLMs show recurring reasoning failures, but with human guidance and oversight can outperform the market.

items.title: QRAFTI: An Agentic Framework for Empirical Research in Quantitative Finance (arXiv)
items.desc: An agentic LLM framework that automates empirical research workflows in quantitative finance.

items.title: Large Language Models and Generative Factor Discovery in Crypto Markets (SSRN)
items.desc: Uses LLMs to generate and discover pricing factors in cryptocurrency markets.

sections.name: 📦 Operations & Supply Chain (INFORMS: Management Science, M&SOM, Operations Research)

items.title: OM Forum — Supply Chain Management in the AI Era: A Vision Statement from the Operations Management Community (M&SOM)
items.desc: 42 OM researchers, practitioners, and technology leaders outline how to combine the structural properties of OM models with machine learning, reinforcement learning, and LLMs across supply chains.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence, Emotional Labor, and Service Operations (M&SOM)
items.desc: Examines how AI adoption reshapes emotional labor and worker-customer interactions in service operations.

items.title: Large Language Model in Creative Work: The Role of Collaboration Modality and User Expertise (Management Science)
items.desc: Published January 2026. Shows how the mode of human-LLM collaboration and the user's expertise level jointly determine the quality of LLM-assisted creative work.

items.title: Dynamics of Cognitive Heterogeneity: Investigating Behavioral Biases in Multi-Stage Supply Chains with LLM-Based Simulation (arXiv)
items.desc: Uses LLM-based agents to simulate how heterogeneous behavioral biases propagate through multi-stage supply chains.

items.title: A $3.2 Trillion Deal-Making Frenzy Is Spurred by the A.I. Economy (NYT, Jul 9)
items.desc: Global deal-making hit ~$3.2T in H1 2026 — up 45% and the biggest half-year in a decade — driven by AI bets, mega-mergers (NextEra-Dominion, SpaceX-Cursor), and AI-linked IPOs; questions remain over whether demand justifies the spend.

items.title: AI has taken over the stock market. The bond market is next (The Economist, Jul 7)
items.desc: Hyperscalers are funding AI with record bond issuance — Morgan Stanley expects $350-400B of AI-related investment-grade issuance in 2026 — while the BIS warns AI projects may not earn enough to repay the debt.

items.title: China may struggle to fund Xi Jinping's tech dreams (The Economist, Jul 9)
items.desc: Despite a capital-markets comeback, China faces obstacles financing its state-led technology and AI ambitions.

items.title: From Cow-Milking Robots to Weed-Zapping Lasers, Farmers Are Embracing A.I. (NYT)
items.desc: How AI-driven robotics and automation are transforming agricultural operations, from dairy barns to weed control.
